strategies.name: Ratio froth
strategies.tagline: The original 165-day shared-base leader, included as a strategy for the same-window comparison.
strategies.summary: No separate treatment; same 2016-2026 window and metrics.

strategies.name: FOMC + post-OpEx window
strategies.tagline: Owns TQQQ in the FOMC intermeeting drift and the post-OpEx flow window, with a volatility throttle.
strategies.summary: Holds TQQQ from FOMC decision +3 through +20 and from monthly OpEx +1 through +3, BIL otherwise, halving exposure when the 20/100-day realised-vol ratio exceeds 1.25. The calendar is hardcoded ex-ante through 2026; the return edge is concentrated in 2020-2023 and it lags calm bulls.

strategies.name: Vol-scaled crash system
strategies.tagline: A stop distance should scale with volatility (0.7 daily ATR) but never widen past the 4% level that protects against gap nights.
strategies.summary: Always-long TQQQ, with an inverse-vol position size and a one-sided ATR barrier that exits to BIL for the rest of the trigger session and the night, should beat the old 165-day base's drawdown with a daily-return correlation below 0.60.

strategies.name: Short-term reversal
strategies.tagline: Buys TQQQ after a two-session down streak or a 3-session drop of at least 1.5%, then holds for a rolling five-session rebound.
strategies.summary: A short-horizon mean-reversion strategy: QQQ down two sessions or down 1.5% over three sessions at the close triggers a TQQQ entry at the next open; the exit rolls forward if another dip signal fires. No trend, stop or vol target in the primary.

strategies.name: Session-timing TQQQ
strategies.tagline: Holds TQQQ from late afternoon through the overnight and opening drive, skipping midday and weak-close nights.
strategies.summary: Enters at 14:30 when TQQQ is up on the session, otherwise at 15:59, holds through the overnight and the next 09:30-10:00, and exits at 10:00; size is scaled by QQQ 10-day vol. The edge is the overnight/opening-drive premium, not a daily trend.

strategies.name: Rebalance-flow de-risk
strategies.tagline: Goes to BIL after a large up day with a strong last 30 minutes, when leveraged-ETF rebalancing is most likely to reverse.
strategies.summary: A mechanical flow strategy: after a big QQQ up day whose last 30 minutes are also up, TQQQ closes with forced rebalancing demand and tends to reverse; the strategy sits in BIL for the next session, otherwise holds a 50%-vol-target TQQQ position.

strategies.name: Fast trend + vol target
strategies.tagline: A 20/50-session QQQ trend gate on TQQQ, sized to an 85% volatility budget with a fast crash brake.
strategies.summary: Holds TQQQ while the fast trend is up, scales the sleeve inversely to realised TQQQ volatility, and exits on a 2.5% intraday stop with a five-session cooldown. The full-window edge is trend and crash timing; the 2019 range-bound bull was a severe whipsaw.

strategies.name: Volatility term structure
strategies.tagline: Splits TQQQ exposure between a 165-day trend sleeve and a RV20/RV60 term-structure sleeve, with an acute-spike kill switch.
strategies.summary: Holds half the book on the QQQ trend and half on a calm term structure (short vol below long vol), drops to cash when short/long vol spikes, and sizes the remainder to the regime. The term structure buys drawdown and Sharpe, not raw CAGR over a simpler trend+spike rule.

strategies.name: ML session-shape
strategies.tagline: A walk-forward weekly ridge model on session-shape price/volume features times TQQQ exposure.
strategies.summary: Uses close-location and volume-ratio features over five-session windows, refits monthly, and holds a vol-targeted TQQQ position when the predicted return exceeds a fraction of the trailing mean. No daily vol/drawdown/trend features in the primary.

strategies.name: Opening-drive intraday
strategies.tagline: Buys TQQQ on a strong opening drive and exits at the close; flat overnight.
strategies.summary: At 09:35, a positive gap plus a positive first five minutes, or at 10:00 a first-30-minute gain above 0.5%, buys TQQQ; an 8% close-based trailing stop exits, otherwise the position is closed at 15:59. No overnight position.

strategies.name: TQQQ/QQQ relative value
strategies.tagline: Holds TQQQ while the TQQQ/QQQ ratio momentum is intact, and falls back to QQQ when leverage is being repriced.
strategies.summary: Uses ratio momentum and QQQ realised volatility to decide whether 3x compounding is being paid for, holding TQQQ in strong regimes and unlevered QQQ otherwise. The ratio signal is almost entirely explained by QQQ trend and variance.

strategies.name: Close-flow exhaustion
strategies.tagline: QQQ down more than 1% by the close forces leveraged-ETF selling into the close; buy the closing print and own the one-session reversal.
strategies.summary: TQQQ bought at the 15:59 print after an orderly intraday QQQ decline outperforms cash over the next session.

strategies.name: OpEx cycle
strategies.tagline: The monthly option-expiry session is the one systematically weak session of the expiry cycle; own the cycle and step out for the expiry session.
strategies.summary: Dealer roll and gamma unwind create a recurring negative intraday drift on the expiry session, so a calendar-only strategy that holds TQQQ around the cycle but never through the expiry session earns a flow premium that is uncorrelated with trend following.

strategies.name: Ratio-cycle standalone
strategies.tagline: The TQQQ/QQQ ratio is a leverage-cycle meter: froth precedes amplified shocks, a deep discount with a turn precedes convex rebounds, and the average state does not pay for 3x drag.
strategies.summary: Hold QQQ by default, cash in ratio froth or variance expansion, and a bounded 40% TQQQ sleeve only after a deep ratio discount turns up.

strategies.name: Closing-pressure overnight carry
strategies.tagline: The overnight+first-30m block pays because it settles the previous session's closing pressure, so it should be held selectively after a sold close rather than every night.
strategies.summary: Block return is decreasing in the last-30-minute QQQ return; conditioning plus a self-referential vol gate beats holding every night.

strategies.name: Unsupervised regime allocator
strategies.tagline: Unsupervised regime clustering allocates TQQQ/QQQ/BIL by each cluster's past forward returns.
strategies.summary: A causal k-means fit on short-horizon market-state features identifies persistent regimes; the historically strongest regime deserves TQQQ, the second QQQ, the rest BIL.

strategies.name: Leverage-decay timing
strategies.tagline: TQQQ's 3x daily reset makes leverage favorable only when the path is smooth; a walk-forward ML classifier of 5-session TQQQ-vs-3xQQQ decay rotates between TQQQ, QQQ and BIL.
strategies.summary: A causal classifier of the worst-quartile 5-session decay can time when to use TQQQ instead of QQQ, and when to hold BIL, with a lower drawdown than the old 165-day TQQQ base and correlation < 0.60.

strategies.name: Time-of-day leverage ladder
strategies.tagline: A weekly three-state leverage ladder on the Nasdaq-100: 3x TQQQ when the overnight-minus-intraday spread and the first-hour return are both above their 26-week medians, 1x QQQ when only one is, and BIL otherwise.
strategies.summary: Weeks with an unusually strong overnight-vs-intraday spread and first-hour momentum have a stronger time-of-day drift; a 3x/1x/0x ladder should beat static QQQ/TQQQ on a risk-adjusted basis with low correlation to the 165-day price-trend base.

strategies.name: Post-capitulation reversal
strategies.tagline: After a >=3% intraday QQQ capitulation, buy TQQQ at the next open and sell before that session's close; flat (BIL) and never overnight otherwise.
strategies.summary: A capitulation session transfers stock from forced sellers to liquidity providers; the compensation is realised in the next session's open-to-close, not in the trigger session or its overnight gap.

strategies.name: Night continuation / day reversal
strategies.tagline: Night continues an up day; the day reverses a down night; size by a 3-sigma gap budget.
strategies.summary: Block-conditional positions capture the overnight/intraday premium without a moving-average regime.

strategies.name: Relative Nasdaq flow dip
strategies.tagline: Nasdaq underperformance vs SPY at the close is temporary LETF/flow pressure; buy TQQQ for a three-session reversal.
strategies.summary: z(QQQ-SPY daily relative return) < -1.25 predicts positive next-three-session TQQQ returns with <0.60 correlation to the old 165-day baseline.

strategies.name: Volatility-state risk parity
strategies.tagline: Equal-risk QQQ/TQQQ composition with a risk budget that rises after transient volatility spikes and is damped in persistent high-vol regimes.
strategies.summary: The conditional Sharpe ratio of the equity factor rises after a transient vol spike and not in a persistent high-vol regime.

strategies.name: Intraday 60-minute trend
strategies.tagline: QQQ's 60-minute EMA cross measures intraday trend persistence; hold TQQQ only while that trend is up and flat overnight.
strategies.summary: An intraday-only, trend-tiered TQQQ position has development correlation below 0.60 with the 165-day overnight base and a positive Sharpe after 5 bp costs.

strategies.name: Quiet capitulation
strategies.tagline: Buy a quiet, short-term-oversold capitulation in QQQ, not a generic gap-down in a 165-day bull regime.
strategies.summary: A large QQQ decline on below-average volume while the market is already 20-day oversold reverses over the next 3 sessions; high-volume declines do not.

strategies.name: Two-stream risk parity
strategies.tagline: Inverse-volatility allocation across two independent return streams: calm QQQ carry (1x) and panic-reversal TQQQ (3x).
strategies.summary: The risk-parity blend earns a positive risk-adjusted return with a lower drawdown than either stream and <0.60 daily correlation with the old 165-day TQQQ baseline.

strategies.name: Participation exhaustion
strategies.tagline: A heavy-volume intraday decline that closes in the upper half of its range marks absorbed supply, so TQQQ rises over the next five sessions.
strategies.summary: Participation-conditioned supply climaxes forecast positive five-session TQQQ returns after costs.

strategies.name: Volatility-shock recovery
strategies.tagline: Volatility-shock recovery: buy TQQQ when a realised-vol shock is decaying inside a market drawdown, sized inversely to vol.
strategies.summary: Post-shock volatility decay marks the end of forced deleveraging; inverse-vol TQQQ captures the recovery with low correlation to the 165-day trend base.

strategies.name: Failed gap-up fade
strategies.tagline: Short QQQ on confirmed failed small gap-ups in a weak, stressed tape.
strategies.summary: The confirmed gap-failure short has positive net expectancy after 1 bp and low correlation with the 165-day base.

strategies.name: LETF overshoot recovery
strategies.tagline: Buy TQQQ after a leveraged-ETF downside overshoot (TQQQ falls >=3% intraday and underperforms 3x QQQ by >=1pp), scaling in 50% then 100% after a recovery close, with a 2% stop and a 3-session hold.
strategies.summary: The relative downside overshoot is a rebalancing/flow effect that reverses over the next 1-3 sessions; a gradual scale-in captures it with low correlation to the 165-day trend base.

strategies.name: Crash-continuation short
strategies.tagline: A 4% break below the TQQQ session open predicts continuation into the close; trade it as an intraday short instead of a long-book exit.
strategies.summary: Shorting TQQQ from the break to the close, flat (BIL) otherwise, earns a positive net return with low correlation to the 165-day long base.

strategies.name: Volatility contraction recovery
strategies.tagline: Volatility spikes mean-revert; the high-vol contraction phase is a distinct TQQQ recovery window, while rising vol from a low is a de-risking signal and QQQ is the default risk asset.
strategies.summary: A daily volatility-percentile/slope state machine with multi-day holds captures a post-spike recovery premium that is not the old 165-day trend base.

strategies.name: Vol-spike reflation
strategies.tagline: Buy a volatility-scaled TQQQ position after a 1-minute-RV spike, an oversold QQQ drawdown and the first up-close; exit on vol normalization, a short time stop or a price stop.
strategies.summary: Post-spike volatility mean reversion plus TQQQ convexity gives a positive 1-3 session rebound that is independent of the 165-day trend.

strategies.name: Deep drawdown recovery
strategies.tagline: After a >=20% QQQ drawdown, own TQQQ only inside a confirmed 60-session recovery window, then stand aside until the drawdown heals.
strategies.summary: The post-capitulation recovery is a distinct, time-limited return state; a confirmed turn after a deep drawdown captures it with low exposure and low correlation to slow trend-following.

strategies.name: Donchian alignment ladder
strategies.tagline: A Donchian breakout is only worth leveraging when short, medium and long breakout horizons agree; the alignment count is the trend/sizing signal.
strategies.summary: Scaling from BIL to QQQ to TQQQ with three-horizon breakout alignment captures trend persistence while cutting whipsaw exposure, with low correlation to the old 165-day MA base.

strategies.name: Opening-range failed-breakdown reclaim
strategies.tagline: A failed breakdown of the 30-minute opening range that reclaims the range low is a liquidity-sweep reversal; buy the reclaim and target the opposite side of the range before the close.
strategies.summary: After a brief break below the opening-range low, the reclaim traps breakout sellers and the reversal continues to the opening-range high; the edge is intraday and independent of the overnight TQQQ drift.

strategies.name: Failed-breakdown spring
strategies.tagline: A failed breakdown / stop-run reclaim: buy TQQQ after QQQ undercuts its prior 20-day low intraday but closes back above it.
strategies.summary: Forced selling from a failed breakdown is exhausted; the next few days tend to rebound, so an event-driven TQQQ long with a 5-day hold beats a pure stop overlay and has low correlation with the old 165-day base.
